comment: I overranked deep normalized rectifiers: E/C isolate activation, and SiLU wins; residual A and zero-LN SiLU D also beat B/C. K1009’s pooled low-progress LN/depth tendency misled my application; K1056 helped identify E, while K1015 warned against architecture-wide ordering. Historical backtest: low-Δ, long-budget piecewise residual models beat deep terminal-LN rectifiers in 6/6 comparisons across two questions; short-budget counterparts won 0/4. Lab comparisons matching optimizer type/rate give only 2/8 residual wins across six low-Δ short-budget piecewise sets, with no low-Δ long-budget matches. Thus trainability depends on activation/topology and budget, not LN count alone. Gradient attenuation versus generalization remains unresolved; no tested rule establishes the complete gold order.
